# Heartbeat security backport: glib 0.18.5

This directory is the `glib` 0.18.5 crates.io archive, SHA-256 `233daaf6e83ae6a12a52055f568f9d7cf4671dabb78ff9560ab6da230ce00ee5`, with one source fix. Its original `LICENSE` and `COPYRIGHT` are retained. The two-line change in `src/variant_iter.rs` backports [gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core#1343](https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core/pull/1343/files) for [RUSTSEC-2024-0429](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2024-0429.html): the out-argument pointer is mutable and passed as `&mut p`. [Debian's patch](https://sources.debian.org/patches/rust-glib-0.18/0.18.5-7/0007-glib-fix-UB-in-VariantStrIter-impl_get.patch/) independently carries the same backport.

`src-tauri/Cargo.toml` selects this local copy with `[patch.crates-io]` for compatible consumers. The package version remains 0.18.5: vulnerability scanners may continue to flag it, and the directory does not fix other defects in the unmaintained GTK3 stack. Do not suppress findings merely because this particular change exists. Review the [security record](../../docs/reviews/security-2026-11-16.md) when advisories or the dependency graph change.

Maintenance: retain the license, source provenance, archive checksum, and this explanation; inspect future `glib` advisories against the vendored code. When Tauri and its Linux GTK/WebKit dependency chain can move to a supported fixed `glib` release, remove the patch section and this directory together, regenerate and review Cargo.lock, rescan, and run Linux and macOS checks. An ARM64 Linux compile and optimized targeted tests do not substitute for an x86_64 Linux build, GUI smoke, or release validation.
